# `sim_engine_builds`

**Tier reference** — project-independent, versioned by vintage rather than by project · owned by `engine` · `public.sim_engine_builds`

**One row is** One row per engine build that produced a result or was reported running, keyed by (engine, code_version). Append-only: `last_seen_at` moves forward, a part the row did not know is filled once, and a build found wrong is WITHDRAWN with a reason, never deleted. The CURRENT build is not stored here — it is `sim_engines.code_version`, which the worker's boot report authors.

## Uniqueness

| Columns | Source | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `engine_id` + `code_version` | UNIQUE constraint | `sim_engine_builds_key` |
| `id` | column PRIMARY KEY | `sim_engine_builds_pkey` |

**Natural key:** `engine_id` + `code_version` — the key this table's grain implies, and the
database ENFORCES it: `sim_engine_builds_key`. A re-upload of the same row updates
it rather than duplicating it.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | **no user-facing write path** |
| Minimum project role | `viewer` |
| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 1 — **1 with no predicate** |

A registry, like `sim_engines`: read by everyone through `sim_engine_builds_read` (`USING (true)`, select only), written by no API role. Its one writer is `_engine_build_record`, internal and service-only (D248), reached three ways: the worker's boot report (`sim_engine_report`), an AFTER trigger on every run row that names its build (the browser writes runs as anon), and the WP 15.2 backfill. The one human act, `sim_engine_build_withdraw`, is super-admin only and records its actor in the row. Not audited: a reference table whose writers name no person, with an append-only trigger instead of an audit trail.

>
> See PLAN.md D28: the application runs as the

> closing these is a migration with an auth model behind it rather than a policy edit.

## Columns

`CSV header` is the name the **user types**, which is not always the column name —
that gap is defect D21. A dash means the column has no CSV origin.

| Column | CSV header | Type | Unit | Required in CSV | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` 🔑 | — | `uuid` | — | — | The build's id within the ledger. A run names its build by `(engine_id, code_version)`, the table's key, not by this id. |
| `engine_id` | — | `uuid` | — | — | The registered engine (`sim_engines`) the build belongs to. |
| `code_version` | — | `text` | — | — | The build, spelled exactly as a run's `code_version` is stamped. Since WP 15.1 it is `scsim-<ENGINE_VERSION>+<12 hex>`, a digest of scsim's source and the worker's compute path, so different code is a different build. A row from before WP 15.1 carries the bare label (`scsim-0.2.8`), which several builds shared; what ran under it is unknown, and the row says so by having no digests. |
| `scsim_digest` | — | `text` | — | — | sha256 over scsim's source files, as the worker reported it. Filled once; NULL for a build no worker reported (a browser run, or history). |
| `sim_worker_digest` | — | `text` | — | — | sha256 over the worker's compute-path modules (`sim_worker/build.py` `COMPUTE_MODULES`). Filled once; NULL as `scsim_digest`. |
| `commit_sha` | — | `text` | — | — | The git commit of the first worker deploy that reported this build. Identical source from a later commit is the same build, so the first commit stands. NULL when no deploy stated one. |
| `image_digest` | — | `text` | — | — | The worker image (Fly) that first reported this build. Filled once. |
| `first_seen_by` | — | `text` | — | — | How the ledger first learned of the build: `worker_report` (the boot report), `run` (a run row named it — the browser's builds arrive this way), or `backfill` (history, WP 15.2). |
| `first_seen_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When the build was first recorded (for backfill, its earliest run). |
| `last_seen_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When a report or a run last named the build. Moves forward only. |
| `withdrawn_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When a super admin withdrew the build. NULL = not withdrawn. Never cleared. |
| `withdrawn_reason` | — | `text` | — | — | Why the build was withdrawn, as stated by the super admin. Shown wherever a result of the build is. |
| `withdrawn_by` | — | `uuid` | — | — | The super admin who withdrew the build (`approved_users`). Set to NULL if that user is later deleted. |
